quizQuestions.prompt: What unusual command did God give Hosea, to picture Israel's unfaithfulness?
quizQuestions.explanation: God told Hosea to marry Gomer, a promiscuous woman, as a living picture of Israel's spiritual unfaithfulness.

options.text: Marry a promiscuous woman named Gomer
Build an altar in a foreign land

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Hosea do after Gomer left him and fell into hardship, showing God's redeeming love?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hosea bought her back, redeeming her, mirroring God's love for unfaithful Israel.

options.text: He asked the king to punish her

quizQuestions.prompt: What did God say He desired more than sacrifice, according to Hosea 6:6, a verse Jesus later quoted?
quizQuestions.explanation: "For I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of God more than burnt offerings."

quizQuestions.prompt: What phrase from Hosea 11:1, about God calling His son out of Egypt, is later applied to Jesus in Matthew's Gospel?
quizQuestions.explanation: "When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt."

quizQuestions.prompt: What symbolic names did Hosea give his children with Gomer?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah ("not pitied"), and Lo-ammi ("not my people") symbolized God's coming judgment.

options.text: Ordinary Hebrew names with no meaning

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hosea 4:6 say God's people are destroyed for lacking?
quizQuestions.explanation: "My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge."

quizQuestions.prompt: Which kingdom of Israel did Hosea primarily prophesy to?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hosea's ministry focused on the northern kingdom of Israel.

options.text: The southern kingdom of Judah only

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise does Hosea 14 give about God healing His people's backsliding?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely."

options.text: He will heal them and love them freely
He will send them to another land
He will send no more prophets

quizQuestions.prompt: What victorious cry against death does Hosea 13:14 give, later quoted by Paul in 1 Corinthians 15?
quizQuestions.explanation: "O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction."

options.text: "O death, I will be thy plagues"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Hosea 2 say God promises to do, betrothing Israel to Himself forever?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I will betroth thee unto me for ever; yea, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness."

options.text: Replace Israel with a new nation

quizQuestions.prompt: What made Hosea's own marriage unique among the prophets' ministries?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hosea's marriage itself became a living illustration of his prophetic message about God and Israel.

options.text: It became a living illustration of his message
He remained unmarried his whole life

quizQuestions.prompt: What overall theme runs through the book of Hosea, comparing Israel's idolatry to something personal?
quizQuestions.explanation: Hosea compares Israel's unfaithfulness to God to spiritual adultery.

quizQuestions.prompt: What devastating event does Joel describe as a picture of coming judgment?
quizQuestions.explanation: A severe locust plague stripped the land bare, pictured as a coming army.

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise from Joel 2:28 did Peter quote at Pentecost about the Holy Spirit?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh."

options.text: "I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh"

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise from Joel 2:32 about calling on the LORD is also quoted in Acts and Romans?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered."

options.text: "Whosoever shall call on the name of the LORD shall be delivered"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Joel 2:13 call the people to rend, instead of just their garments, as true repentance?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God."

quizQuestions.prompt: What recurring phrase describes the coming judgment throughout the book of Joel?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The day of the LORD" is a central, recurring phrase in Joel.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Joel 3:10 call the nations to beat their plowshares into, the opposite of Isaiah's image of peace?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Beat your plowshares into swords" — a call to war, contrasting Isaiah's vision of peace.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Joel 2:25 promise God will restore, after the locust devastation?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten."

quizQuestions.prompt: Which New Testament apostle quoted Joel extensively in his famous Pentecost sermon?
quizQuestions.explanation: Peter quoted Joel's prophecy about the outpouring of the Spirit in Acts 2.

quizQuestions.prompt: What was Amos's occupation before God called him to prophesy?
quizQuestions.explanation: Amos was a shepherd/herdsman from Tekoa.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Amos say about his background when accused of being a professional prophet for money?
quizQuestions.explanation: He said he was no prophet nor a prophet's son, but the LORD took him from following the flock.

options.text: He was no prophet's son, just a shepherd God called
He was trained at the Temple school
He was the son of a prophet

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Amos 5:24 call for, using the image of running water?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream."

options.text: Judgment and righteousness like flowing water
A new temple by the river

quizQuestions.prompt: What social issue did Amos's prophecies focus heavily on condemning?
quizQuestions.explanation: Amos condemned social injustice, especially oppression of the poor by the wealthy.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Amos 3:7 say God does before acting, regarding His prophets?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Surely the Lord GOD will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets."

options.text: He reveals His plans to His prophets first
He waits for kings to ask

quizQuestions.prompt: What kind of famine does Amos 8:11 say is coming, unlike a normal famine?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD."

options.text: A famine of hearing God's word
A famine of silver and gold

quizQuestions.prompt: Though Amos was from Judah, which kingdom did he primarily prophesy against?
quizQuestions.explanation: Amos was sent to prophesy primarily against the northern kingdom of Israel.

quizQuestions.prompt: What warning does Amos 4:12 give Israel about meeting God?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Prepare to meet thy God, O Israel."

quizQuestions.prompt: What building tool did God show Amos in a vision, symbolizing Israel's crookedness?
quizQuestions.explanation: God showed Amos a plumbline, showing how far Israel had strayed from His standard.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Amos 9:11 promise God will raise up again, a sign of future restoration?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I will raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen."

quizQuestions.prompt: How does the book of Amos begin, before turning its focus to Israel itself?
quizQuestions.explanation: It opens with judgments pronounced against the nations surrounding Israel.

quizQuestions.prompt: What warning does Amos 6:1 give against complacency among the comfortable?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Woe to them that are at ease in Zion."

options.text: "Woe to them that are at ease in Zion"
"Come unto me, all ye that labour"

quizQuestions.prompt: Which nation, descended from Esau, is Obadiah's entire prophecy directed against?
quizQuestions.explanation: Obadiah's short prophecy is entirely a judgment against Edom.

quizQuestions.prompt: What sin does Obadiah 1:10 accuse Edom of, regarding their brother nation Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Edom is condemned for violence against Jacob (Israel) and for gloating over Judah's disaster.

options.text: Violence against and gloating over Israel's disaster
Stealing the Ark of the Covenant

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Obadiah 1:3 say deceived Edom, dwelling securely in mountain clefts?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock."

quizQuestions.prompt: What principle does Obadiah 1:15 declare about the day of the LORD, regarding how nations are treated?
quizQuestions.explanation: "As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head."

options.text: As you have done, it shall be done to you
All nations will be spared equally
Only Edom will ever be judged

quizQuestions.prompt: How does the book of Obadiah conclude, regarding who the kingdom will ultimately belong to?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The kingdom shall be the LORD's."

quizQuestions.prompt: How many chapters does the book of Obadiah contain, making it the shortest book in the Old Testament?
quizQuestions.explanation: Obadiah has just one chapter, 21 verses total.

quizQuestions.prompt: What city did God call Jonah to preach to, which Jonah tried to avoid?
quizQuestions.explanation: God called Jonah to preach to Nineveh, a great and wicked city.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jonah do instead of obeying God's call to preach to Nineveh?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jonah fled in the opposite direction, boarding a ship toward Tarshish.

options.text: He fled by ship toward Tarshish
He asked another prophet to go

quizQuestions.prompt: How did the sailors on Jonah's ship determine that he was the cause of the dangerous storm?
quizQuestions.explanation: The sailors cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.

options.text: They asked the captain to guess

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Jonah after the sailors threw him overboard to calm the storm?
quizQuestions.explanation: A great fish swallowed Jonah, and he was inside it three days and three nights.

options.text: He was rescued by another ship

quizQuestions.prompt: How long was Jonah inside the great fish?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jonah do while inside the fish?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jonah prayed to God from inside the fish, acknowledging his need for deliverance.

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to Jonah after the fish had him for three days?
quizQuestions.explanation: The fish vomited Jonah out onto dry land.

options.text: The fish vomited him onto dry land
The fish carried him to Nineveh

quizQuestions.prompt: What message did Jonah finally preach to Nineveh?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown."

options.text: "Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown"
"Repent, for the kingdom is at hand"

quizQuestions.prompt: How did the city of Nineveh respond to Jonah's message?
quizQuestions.explanation: The whole city repented, fasting and wearing sackcloth, from the king down to the least.

quizQuestions.prompt: Who joined the people of Nineveh in fasting and wearing sackcloth after Jonah's message?
quizQuestions.explanation: Even the king of Nineveh put on sackcloth and called for a fast.

quizQuestions.prompt: How did Jonah feel about God sparing Nineveh instead of destroying it?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jonah became angry, upset that God showed mercy to a wicked city.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did God provide to teach Jonah a lesson about compassion, a plant that later withered?
quizQuestions.explanation: God provided a plant (gourd) to shade Jonah, then sent a worm to destroy it.

options.text: A plant that gave shade, then withered
A tree that bore fruit instantly

quizQuestions.prompt: What closing question does God ask Jonah about Nineveh, ending the book?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Should not I spare Nineveh, that great city?"

options.text: "Should not I spare Nineveh, that great city?"
"Who told thee to go to Tarshish?"

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Jesus later compare His own coming death and resurrection to, referencing Jonah's story?
quizQuestions.explanation: Jesus said, "as Jonah was three days and three nights in the whale's belly," so He would be in the earth.

options.text: Jonah's three days in the fish

quizQuestions.prompt: What town did Micah prophesy would be the birthplace of a future ruler over Israel?
quizQuestions.explanation: Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem as the Messiah's birthplace, fulfilled in Jesus.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Micah 6:8 say the LORD requires of a person?
quizQuestions.explanation: "To do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God."

options.text: Do justly, love mercy, walk humbly with God

quizQuestions.prompt: Which chief priests and scribes quoted Micah's Bethlehem prophecy when King Herod asked where the Christ would be born?
quizQuestions.explanation: They quoted Micah 5:2 in answer to Herod's question, recorded in Matthew 2.

options.text: The chief priests and scribes of Herod's court
The wise men from the East

quizQuestions.prompt: What vision of future peace does Micah 4 share almost word-for-word with Isaiah, about weapons becoming farm tools?
quizQuestions.explanation: Micah 4:3, like Isaiah 2:4, prophesies swords being beaten into plowshares.

quizQuestions.prompt: During the reigns of which kings of Judah did Micah prophesy?
quizQuestions.explanation: Micah's ministry spanned the reigns of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Micah 7:18 ask about God, comparing Him to no one else, regarding forgiveness?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity?"

options.text: "Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity?"
"Who has known the mind of the LORD?"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Micah 7:19 say God will do with His people's sins, casting them somewhere far away?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea."

options.text: Cast them into the depths of the sea

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Micah prophesy would happen to Zion/Jerusalem because of corrupt leaders?
quizQuestions.explanation: Micah warned Zion would be plowed like a field because of corrupt rulers, priests, and prophets.

options.text: It would be plowed like a field
It would be given a new king immediately
It would become the world's capital

quizQuestions.prompt: What corrupt practice among judges and prophets did Micah specifically condemn?
quizQuestions.explanation: Micah condemned leaders who judged for bribes and prophesied for money.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Micah's own name mean, reflecting the closing praise of his book?
quizQuestions.explanation: Micah's name means "Who is like the LORD?" — echoed in his closing praise of God's mercy.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which great city does Nahum's entire prophecy pronounce judgment against?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nahum's short book is entirely a prophecy of judgment against Nineveh.

quizQuestions.prompt: What earlier event, generations before Nahum, had spared the same city he now announces judgment on?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nineveh had repented under Jonah's preaching generations earlier, but had returned to wickedness by Nahum's time.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Nahum 1:3 say about the LORD's patience and justice together?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power, and will not at all acquit the wicked."

options.text: Slow to anger, but will not acquit the wicked
Quick to anger and quick to forgive

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Nahum 1:7 call the LORD, offering comfort in trouble?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The LORD is good, a strong hold in the day of trouble."

options.text: A strong hold in the day of trouble

quizQuestions.prompt: What title does Nahum 3:1 give Nineveh, describing its violence and deceit?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nahum calls Nineveh "the bloody city," full of lies and robbery.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does the book of Nahum describe in vivid detail regarding Nineveh's future?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nahum vividly describes the coming destruction and plunder of Nineveh.

options.text: Its rebuilding into a greater city
Its conversion to worship the LORD

quizQuestions.prompt: Which empire was Nineveh the capital of, the great power Nahum's prophecy concerns?
quizQuestions.explanation: Nineveh was the capital of the Assyrian Empire.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Habakkuk question God about at the very start of the book?
quizQuestions.explanation: Habakkuk asks God how long he must cry out about violence and injustice going unanswered.

options.text: Why violence and injustice go unanswered
Why he was chosen as a prophet

quizQuestions.prompt: What empire does God tell Habakkuk He is raising up to bring judgment on Judah?
quizQuestions.explanation: God answers that He is raising up the Chaldeans (Babylonians).

quizQuestions.prompt: What famous statement from Habakkuk 2:4 is later quoted three times in the New Testament?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The just shall live by his faith" is quoted in Romans, Galatians, and Hebrews.

options.text: "The just shall live by his faith"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Habakkuk 2:20 say all the earth should do before the LORD in His holy temple?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The LORD is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him."

quizQuestions.prompt: How does the book of Habakkuk end, despite the prophet's earlier hard questions?
quizQuestions.explanation: It ends with a prayer/psalm of trust and joy in God, even amid hardship.

options.text: A psalm of trust and joy in God

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Habakkuk say he will do even if the fig tree does not blossom and the flocks are gone?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Yet I will rejoice in the LORD, I will joy in the God of my salvation."

quizQuestions.prompt: What structure makes Habakkuk unique among the prophetic books?
quizQuestions.explanation: Much of Habakkuk is structured as a dialogue between the prophet's honest complaints and God's answers.

options.text: A dialogue between the prophet and God

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Habakkuk say he will do while watching for God's answer to his complaint?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me."

quizQuestions.prompt: During the reign of which reforming king of Judah did Zephaniah prophesy?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zephaniah prophesied during the reign of Josiah.

quizQuestions.prompt: What recurring theme does Zephaniah describe as near and terrible?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The great day of the LORD is near" is a central theme of Zephaniah.

options.text: The great day of the LORD
The coronation of a new king

quizQuestions.prompt: What comforting promise does Zephaniah 3:17 give, that God will rejoice over His people with singing?
quizQuestions.explanation: "He will save, he will joy over thee with singing."

options.text: God will rejoice over His people with singing

quizQuestions.prompt: How does the book of Zephaniah open, in terms of the scope of the coming judgment?
quizQuestions.explanation: It opens with sweeping judgment described against all creation because of sin.

quizQuestions.prompt: Which nations does Zephaniah 2 call out for coming judgment, alongside Judah?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zephaniah pronounces judgment on the Philistines, Moab, Ammon, Ethiopia, and Assyria.

options.text: Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Ethiopia, and Assyria

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Zephaniah 3:9 promise God will give the peoples, so all may call on Him together?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I will turn to the people a pure language, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD."

quizQuestions.prompt: Zephaniah's opening verse identifies him as a descendant of which earlier king of Judah?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zephaniah's genealogy is traced back to King Hezekiah.

quizQuestions.prompt: What project did Haggai's prophecies urge the returned exiles to complete?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haggai urged the people to resume rebuilding the Temple in Jerusalem.

quizQuestions.prompt: What did Haggai rebuke the people for, while the Temple lay unfinished?
quizQuestions.explanation: He rebuked them for living comfortably in their own paneled houses while God's house lay in ruins.

options.text: Living comfortably while the Temple lay in ruins

quizQuestions.prompt: To which two leaders did Haggai direct his prophecies, the governor and the high priest?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haggai prophesied to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest.

quizQuestions.prompt: What promise does Haggai 2:9 give about the glory of the new Temple compared to the former one?
quizQuestions.explanation: "The glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former."

options.text: It would be greater than the former Temple's glory
It would be smaller and less glorious
It would be destroyed again immediately

quizQuestions.prompt: What happened to the people's motivation after hearing Haggai's message?
quizQuestions.explanation: Their spirits were stirred, and they resumed work on the Temple.

options.text: Their spirits were stirred to resume the work
They ignored him and left Jerusalem

quizQuestions.prompt: Haggai's ministry is precisely dated to the reign of which Persian king?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haggai's prophecies are dated to the second year of King Darius.

quizQuestions.prompt: How many chapters does the short book of Haggai contain?
quizQuestions.explanation: Haggai has just two chapters.

quizQuestions.prompt: What prophecy from Zechariah 9:9 describes a coming king entering Jerusalem on a donkey?
quizQuestions.explanation: This prophecy was fulfilled in Jesus' triumphal entry into Jerusalem.

options.text: A king coming lowly, riding on a donkey
A king arriving on a great warhorse
A king carried on a golden throne
A king walking barefoot in sackcloth

quizQuestions.prompt: What amount of silver does Zechariah 11:12-13 prophesy, later echoed in Judas' betrayal of Jesus?
quizQuestions.explanation: Thirty pieces of silver, later paralleled in Judas' payment for betraying Jesus.

quizQuestions.prompt: What famous phrase from Zechariah 4:6 describes how God's work is accomplished, not by human strength?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the LORD of hosts."

options.text: "Not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit"

quizQuestions.prompt: Alongside which other prophet did Zechariah encourage the returned exiles to rebuild the Temple?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zechariah prophesied alongside Haggai, both urging the Temple's completion.

quizQuestions.prompt: In Zechariah's vision, what happened to Joshua the high priest's filthy garments?
quizQuestions.explanation: His filthy garments were removed, and he was clothed with clean, rich apparel.

options.text: They were removed and replaced with clean robes
They were given to a stranger

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Zechariah 12:10 prophesy people will do when they look on the one they pierced?
quizQuestions.explanation: "They shall look upon me whom they have pierced, and they shall mourn for him."

quizQuestions.prompt: What title does Zechariah 6:12-13 give to a coming figure who would build the Temple and be both king and priest?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zechariah calls this figure "the Branch," prophetically pointing to the Messiah.

quizQuestions.prompt: What practical instruction does Zechariah 8:16 give about how neighbors should treat each other?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Speak ye every man the truth to his neighbour."

options.text: Speak the truth to one another

quizQuestions.prompt: Besides being a prophet, what other role did Zechariah hold, like Jeremiah and Ezekiel before him?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zechariah was also a priest, from a priestly family.

quizQuestions.prompt: What does the final chapter of Zechariah say will happen at the Mount of Olives on the day of final battle?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zechariah 14 describes the LORD's feet standing on the Mount of Olives, which splits in two.

options.text: The LORD's feet will stand there, and it will split
A new temple will instantly appear
All nations will gather in peace

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Zechariah's own name mean, reflecting a recurring hope throughout his book?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zechariah's name means "the LORD remembers."

quizQuestions.prompt: What symbolic vision involving four horns and four craftsmen appears early in Zechariah's series of night visions?
quizQuestions.explanation: Zechariah saw four horns (representing powers that scattered Judah) and four craftsmen sent to terrify and cast them out.

quizQuestions.prompt: What issue among the priests does Malachi rebuke, regarding sacrifices?
quizQuestions.explanation: Malachi rebukes the priests for offering blemished, defiled sacrifices instead of their best.

options.text: Refusing to offer sacrifices at all

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Malachi 3:8 accuse the people of doing to God, by withholding tithes and offerings?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Will a man rob God? Yet ye have robbed me... in tithes and offerings."

quizQuestions.prompt: What challenge does Malachi 3:10 give the people, about bringing tithes into the storehouse?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse... and prove me now herewith, saith the LORD of hosts."

quizQuestions.prompt: Who does Malachi 4:5-6 prophesy will come before the great and dreadful day of the LORD, understood to point to John the Baptist?
quizQuestions.explanation: Malachi prophesies the coming of "Elijah the prophet" to turn the hearts of fathers to children.

quizQuestions.prompt: What striking declaration does God make in Malachi 1:2-3 about Jacob and Esau?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I have loved Jacob, and I hated Esau" — describing God's sovereign choice.

options.text: "I have loved Jacob, and I hated Esau"

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Malachi 3:1 prophesy God will send to prepare the way before the LORD?
quizQuestions.explanation: "Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me."

quizQuestions.prompt: What does Malachi 3:6 say about God's nature, that gives His people hope despite their unfaithfulness?
quizQuestions.explanation: "I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed."

options.text: "I am the LORD, I change not"
"I will start anew with a new people"

quizQuestions.prompt: What relational sin does Malachi 2 rebuke among the men of Judah, involving treachery toward their wives?
quizQuestions.explanation: Malachi condemns treacherous divorce and unfaithfulness to the wives of their youth.

quizQuestions.prompt: What comparison does Malachi 1:6 use to rebuke the priests for their disrespect toward God?
quizQuestions.explanation: God compares Himself to a father who deserves honor, as a priest disrespecting Him would a father.

options.text: A father who deserves honor from a son
A king who has no subjects

quizQuestions.prompt: What position does Malachi hold in the ordering of the Christian Old Testament?
quizQuestions.explanation: Malachi is the final book of the Old Testament, closing out its 39 books before the New Testament begins.

options.text: The final book of the Old Testament
The first book of the Old Testament
The middle book of the Pentateuch
The first book of the New Testament

quizQuestions.prompt: How many total books make up the Old Testament in the Protestant Bible, which Malachi closes out?
quizQuestions.explanation: The Protestant Old Testament contains 39 books, from Genesis to Malachi.
